title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: The homeowner provides identified personal data (account credentials, device information) when registering and enrolling cameras/sensors on the Home Hub.

title: Unique identifier in registration data
description: The registration process involves unique identifiers that can be used to identify the homeowner and link to their enrolled devices.

title: Data subject distinguishability
description: The homeowner's registration data combined with device enrollment information could make the data subject distinguishable from other users.

title: Attributable data evidence
description: The registration data and actions can be attributed to the homeowner, preventing them from denying certain claims about their account and device enrollment.

title: Observed communications
description: The data flow between homeowner and Home Hub could be observed by third parties, potentially revealing sensitive information about the homeowner's devices and activities.

title: Data type sensitivity
description: The homeowner may provide more sensitive data types than functionally required for basic account registration and device enrollment.

title: Excessive volume of data
description: The homeowner may provide more personal data than functionally needed for the registration and enrollment process.

title: Unnecessary data treatment
description: The Home Hub may process, analyze, or enrich the registration data in ways that are not necessary to achieve the functional goals of the system.

title: Excessive party access
description: The Home Hub may make registration and device data accessible to more parties than functionally necessary.

title: Unawareness of processing
description: The homeowner may not be fully aware of how their registration data and device information will be collected, processed, and stored.

title: Lack of preference control
description: The homeowner may lack control over how their personal data is processed, stored, or shared after registration.

title: Insufficient data subject controls
description: The Home Hub may not provide adequate support for data subject rights such as access, rectification, and erasure of personal data.

title: Violation of data minimization
description: The homeowner may provide more personal data than is actually needed for the registration and device enrollment process.

title: Guest access code as unique identifier
description: The temporary access code entered by the guest serves as a unique reference to the guest's identity, enabling identification of the data subject.
assumptions: The access code is unique to the guest and can be traced back to their identity.

title: Access code enables linking through identifiers
description: The access code in transit can be used as an identifier to link the guest to other data or activities, potentially enabling cross-referencing with other systems.
assumptions: The access code is transmitted in a way that preserves its unique identifier properties.

title: Processing of identified data
description: The Home Hub processes the access code as identified data, which may be stored or logged for future reference.
assumptions: The system retains records of access codes for security or audit purposes.

title: Data type sensitivity - access code may be more sensitive than needed
description: The access code may be more sensitive than functionally required for door unlocking, as it could potentially be used to identify the guest beyond the immediate access purpose.
assumptions: The access code could be used to identify the guest beyond the immediate door access function.

title: Guest unawareness of processing
description: The guest may not be aware that their access code is being logged, stored, or used for purposes beyond the immediate door unlocking function.
assumptions: The guest does not have explicit knowledge of how their access code is processed and stored.

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The system may process more personal data than is actually needed for the functional goal of unlocking the door, potentially including access code metadata or logs.
assumptions: The system collects and processes more data than strictly required for door access functionality.

title: Linking through unique identifier in camera data
description: Camera clips may contain unique identifiers (timestamps, device IDs, location data) that can be used to link video data to specific individuals or households.

title: Processing of unique identifiers in video data
description: The home hub processes video data containing unique references to the identity of the data subject (e.g., device ID, timestamp, location).

title: Collection of more sensitive data than functionally required
description: Camera clips may include more sensitive data types than functionally required for the video upload functionality (e.g., full video vs. metadata only).

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combining
description: Video data in transit may be combined with other data (timestamps, location, user account) to link to specific individuals.

title: Identified information in metadata
description: Metadata of the video files in transit may contain identified information (timestamps, device identifiers, location data).

title: Data accessible to more parties than functionally necessary
description: Cloud video storage may make video data accessible to more parties (e.g., cloud service providers, third-party analytics) than functionally necessary for storage.

title: Personal data kept longer than functionally needed
description: Cloud storage may retain video data longer than functionally needed for the video upload functionality.

title: Revealing attributes in stored video data
description: Stored video data may contain revealing attributes that support identification of the data subject (faces, license plates, etc.).

title: Linking through motion alert metadata
description: Motion alert data in transit may contain metadata (timestamps, device identifiers, location coordinates) that can be used to link the alert to a specific individual or household, enabling cross-referencing with other data sources.
assumptions: Assumes motion alerts may include device identifiers or location data that could be used for linking purposes.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if motion alerts include identifying metadata - depends on implementation details.

title: Identifying information in motion alert
description: Home Hub may include device identifiers or unique references to the data subject in the motion alert data being shared with the mobile app backend.
assumptions: Assumes motion alerts may contain device identifiers or unique references to the data subject.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if motion alerts include identifying information - depends on implementation details.

title: Potentially unnecessary data types in motion alert
description: Home Hub may include more sensitive data types in the motion alert than functionally required for the alerting purpose (e.g., detailed location coordinates, device specifications).
assumptions: Assumes motion alerts may include more data than strictly necessary for the alerting function.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain what data types are included in motion alerts - depends on implementation.

title: Data propagation to mobile app services
description: Mobile App Backend may propagate motion alert data to other services or systems where it is not functionally needed, increasing exposure risk.
assumptions: Assumes mobile app backend may share data with other services beyond the immediate alerting function.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain what additional services the mobile app backend may access - depends on system architecture.

title: Unawareness of motion alert processing
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their motion data is being collected, processed, and shared with the mobile app backend for alerting purposes.
assumptions: Assumes data subjects may not have explicit knowledge of the motion alert processing flow.
uncertainty_note: Uncertain if data subjects are aware of the motion alert processing - depends on notification practices.

title: Profiling of individuals through device-usage analytics
description: Aggregated device-usage analytics may contain patterns that can be used to profile individual users, potentially linking behavioral patterns to specific individuals through inference and analysis.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics vendor has access to sufficient data to perform profiling analysis

title: Revealing attributes in device-usage data
description: Device-usage analytics may include revealing attributes (such as device type, usage patterns, or timing information) that can support the identification of data subjects even when aggregated.
assumptions: Assumes device-usage data contains attributes that can be used to identify or distinguish individuals

title: Potentially sensitive data types collected
description: Device-usage analytics may include data types that are more sensitive than functionally required for the analytics purpose, such as detailed usage patterns or timing information.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics purpose does not require all collected data types

title: Unawareness of data sharing with analytics vendor
description: Data subjects may not be aware that their device-usage analytics are being shared with external analytics vendors, violating transparency requirements.
assumptions: Assumes users are not explicitly informed about this specific data sharing

title: Lack of user control over data sharing preferences
description: Users may not have meaningful control over whether their device-usage analytics are shared with external analytics vendors or with whom.
assumptions: Assumes the app does not provide granular consent controls for analytics sharing

title: Linking through quasi-identifier combination in data flow
description: The data flow itself may contain quasi-identifiers (device IDs, usage patterns, timestamps) that can be combined with other data sources to link to specific individuals.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow contains attributes that can serve as quasi-identifiers

title: Propagation of analytics data to other services
description: The analytics vendor may propagate the received device-usage analytics to other services or partners where it is not functionally needed.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor may share data with third parties beyond the original purpose

title: Violation of data minimization principle
description: The analytics vendor may process more personal data than is actually needed for the analytics functionality, violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: Assumes the vendor may collect and process more data than functionally required

title: Video metadata enables linking through unique identifiers
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may contain unique identifiers (timestamps, location data, user IDs) that can be used to link the homeowner to other data sources or activities.
assumptions: Video metadata is preserved during storage and retrieval

title: Video metadata in transit enables quasi-identifier linking
description: Video metadata transmitted during the data flow (timestamps, location, user ID) can be used to link the homeowner to other data sources through quasi-identifier combination.
assumptions: Metadata is transmitted with the video data

title: Video data contains unique identifiers for the data subject
description: The mobile app backend processes video data that contains unique references to the homeowner's identity (user ID, account information).
assumptions: Video data includes user identification information

title: Video data type sensitivity exceeds functional requirements
description: Video clips may contain highly sensitive personal data (home environment, activities) that should only be processed when strictly required for playback functionality.
assumptions: Video content may reveal sensitive personal information

title: Homeowner unaware of video data processing
description: The homeowner may not be aware that their video data is being processed, stored, or potentially disclosed beyond the playback functionality.
assumptions: Homeowner consent and awareness is not guaranteed

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Processing video data may involve more personal data than actually needed for the playback functionality, potentially violating GDPR data minimization requirements.
assumptions: GDPR or similar privacy regulations apply
